 Federal Governors urge Congress to increase LIHEAP funding
 Liz Carey 
 | 
 November 12, 2026 
 | 
 2 min read 
 In a letter to Congressional leadership, governors across New England asked for more federal funding for the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) citing increases in fuel costs.
 The six governors, from Maine, Rhode Island, Vermont, Connecticut, New Hampshire and Massachusetts requested an additional $3 billion in LIHEAP funding to help vulnerable households stay warm amid sharply rising energy costs. Homes in New England have some of the highest rates of reliance on deliverable oil in the country and are expected to struggle this winter due to dramatic price increases in the cost of oil. The governors stressed Congress needs to take action soon as winter approaches and many households are expected to struggle to afford to heat their homes.
 “More than one third of households in Connecticut depend on deliverable oil to heat their homes. As oil prices spike and temperatures drop, these families—many of whom are already living on tight budgets—are going to struggle to fill up their fuel tanks due to international factors that are no fault of their own,” Connecticut Gov. Ned Lamont said. “With winter approaching, we ask that Congress allocate additional federal funds for this extremely important home heating assistance program.”
 Lamont said he released $12.7 million in emergency state aid from his state’s Federal Cuts Response Fund to supplement Connecticut’s allocation of federal LIHEAP funding. But the dramatic price increases in electricity and oil are still expected to impact homes across his state, and across the country.
